items.sentence: Cuando era niño, ___ al parque todos los días.
items.note: Imperfect (iba) for repeated past actions — “I used to go.”

items.sentence: Busco un apartamento que ___ dos habitaciones.
items.note: Subjunctive (tenga) after “que” when describing something uncertain.
Para marks purpose or a recipient — para ti = “for you.”
Preterite (llegué) for a single, completed past action.

items.sentence: Quand j’étais petit, j’___ souvent à la plage.
items.note: Imparfait (allais) for repeated or habitual past actions.

items.sentence: Il faut que tu ___ au marché.
items.note: Subjunctive (ailles) is required after il faut que.
De marks origin — vient de Londres = “comes from London.”

items.sentence: Il ___ ce livre depuis une heure.
items.note: Present + depuis marks an action still going on — “has been reading.”
Imperfetto (andavo) for habitual actions in the past.
Congiuntivo (sia) after penso che — opinions trigger the subjunctive.
Alla combines a + la before a feminine noun like stazione.
Passato prossimo (sono andato) for a single completed event.
Estava (imperfect of estar) describes a temporary state in the past, not a permanent quality.
Subjunctive (goste) after espero que — hopes trigger it.

items.sentence: Quando eu era criança, ___ futebol todos os domingos.
items.note: Imperfeito (jogava) for a repeated childhood habit.
Da = de + a, contracted before a feminine noun like estação.
は marks the topic — “as for this, it’s interesting.”
を marks the direct object of 書く (to write) — here, in the past tense.

items.sentence: {友達|ともだち}___プレゼントをあげました。
items.note: に marks the target of an action — “to” a friend.
が marks the subject before an adjective like 近い.
已经 (already) pairs with 过 to show a completed experience.
比 is the comparison marker — A 比 B = “A is more than B.”
把 moves the object before the verb when there’s a clear result.
是 is the linking verb “to be” between two nouns.
